description:
Programme or Project Overview

Amsterdam UMC is recruiting a PhD candidate for a project on the epidemiology of kidney replacement therapy in Europe. The project studies how dialysis and transplantation are provided, used and experienced across European countries, and what explains differences in access, outcomes and quality of life for patients on kidney replacement therapy.

The doctoral candidate will work with European registry data and cohort materials, apply comparative epidemiological methods, and contribute to publications and reports aimed at both clinical and policy audiences. The position is embedded in the centre's nephrology and epidemiology research environment, and recruitment is rolling, with applications reviewed as they arrive.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in epidemiology, public health, medicine, health sciences or a related quantitative discipline. Strong statistical and data-management skills and an interest in international comparative research are essential. The appointment is a salaried PhD track under the CAO-UMC collective agreement with a gross monthly salary between EUR 3,217 and EUR 4,077, and the working language is English.

Highlights

  • Epidemiology of kidney replacement therapy
  • European registry and cohort data analysis
  • Comparative health-services research
  • Access, outcomes and quality of life in dialysis and transplantation
  • Research aimed at clinical and policy audiences
  • Salaried PhD, EUR 3,217 - 4,077 per month (CAO-UMC)

About Amsterdam UMC

Amsterdam UMC is the combined academic medical centre of the University of Amsterdam and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, operating from AMC and VUmc campuses. It is one of the largest biomedical research institutions in the Netherlands, with research programmes spanning infectious diseases, oncology, cardiovascular science, epidemiology, public health and health data science. The centre employs PhD candidates and postdocs on salaried contracts under the CAO-UMC collective agreement. Research vacancies are published on the werkenbij.amsterdamumc.org portal, and many doctoral projects are embedded in national and European research consortia.
